    Retain the exact contract-v3 PPO package from r1202 and accepted gate r1232. The provided reconstruction r0002 and fixed criteria r0003 guided opposed acquisition, an active in-hand turn and controlled supported release. The v10 feasibility gate gives 27 of 32. Independent final gate r1239 gives 63 of 64 with zero simulated hardware violations or stops, and the cumulative fresh suite gives 285 of 288. Final verification r1303 associates that exact model and manifest with the latest evidence. All 13 target rounds have judgments and sent-command replays. The exact retained package gives two clean target trials in [redacted] and one in [redacted], so target mastery remains unmet. The frozen v10 model retains all eight first grasps in [redacted] replay while two persist on the target. It also misses the two upper middle MCP2 excursions and the retry torque halt. The load-dependent middle contact calibration improved earlier held-out motion and preserved established replay paths. The later contact changes repair isolated support sequences and lose prior successful paths. The randomized-cap, loaded-opening and supported-slide PPO comparisons improve selected sensitivities and fail to displace the incumbent on the frozen suite. Given more target access, I would collect independent timed contact and actuator-response traces around the early supported displacement and the retry, then fit both finger-limit and arm-moment response against held-out starts. I would test the resulting first grasp and recovery trajectories before freezing a further simulator version. The measured target gaps and the verified simulation outcome are recorded separately.

Criteria text

Plug manipulation verification criteria, version 1

Evidence and scope

The 30 Hz video and reconstruction r0002 show two sequential cycles. Deployment uses one white station plug. The white cycle is the primary reference, and the black cycle confirms the order and the change in wrist and finger pose. Frame numbers below are zero-based. Measurements come from given/recon/analysis/reference_states.npz and the phase labels in given/recon/analysis/analysis.json.

White-plug frames and video timeVisible eventReconstruction estimate
36–70, 1.20–2.33 sAn open right hand approaches from above, with the back of the hand above the fingers.Palm-side normal is 12° from down at frame 70. Absolute approach wrist pose is less reliable while the hand enters the frame.
71–99, 2.37–3.30 sThe thumb closes against opposing fingers on the housing.Pose stays at the supported start. Palm-side normal is 7° from down at the start and 6° at the end.
100–109, 3.33–3.63 sThe hand lifts the plug before the major turn.Housing centre rises 7 mm during this interval and peaks 25 mm above its start during the turn. Reconstructed clearance is partly inferred under occlusion.
110–143, 3.67–4.77 sThumb and index/middle change flexion and contact as the blades turn up. Translation to the left begins during the turn.Plug rotates 115° in world and 88° relative to wrist between endpoints. Wrist rotates 27° between endpoints and swings at most 45° across frames 100–185. The normal tilts from 14° to 34° from down during the turn.
144–161, 4.80–5.37 sThe hand continues left with blades up.+Z is already vertical. The plug travels a further 56 mm toward +y from frame 143 to 162.
162–215, 5.40–7.17 sThe hand lowers the plug onto its back face, opens, and withdraws.Palm-side normal is about 40° from down at placement. The final centre is 199 mm toward +y from its start, with the blades vertical. It remains standing through the rest of the 14.53 s video.

The black plug travels 212 mm toward +y, peaks 29 mm above start and turns 98° relative to the wrist across frames 280–355. Its approach is more oblique, with its palm-side normal roughly 48° from down just before lift. The inferred normal is negative MANO wrist +Y. Its robot counterpart is Wuji palm +X. The fitted contact timings and precise forces are uncertain. The criteria use simulation contacts and measured robot motion where the video cannot resolve those details.

Ordered stages

  1. Lift. Begin with the plug supported on its deployment face. Make thumb plus opposing-finger contact with the palm-side normal within 45° of world down and the plug still supported or just lifting. Then keep an opposed grip off the table for at least 0.10 s, rising at least 10 mm above initial centre height within that grip. The white grasp was about 7° from down. The 45° tolerance allows approach adjustments within the robot's reachable workspace and preserves an above-table approach. The 10 mm rise is below the measured 25 mm airborne peak and clears initial contact and small support-pose errors. The 0.10 s interval is the shortest counted by the standard measurement and excludes momentary collision. Standard predicates are opposed_s >= 0.10 and max_rise_m >= 0.010.
  2. Turn. Continue in an opposed, unsupported grip. The object must rotate at least 50° relative to the palm before reaching blades within 20° of up in that grip. The peak wrist rotation within the successful opposed interval must be at most 65°, close to the observed 45° white/54° black swing with allowance for robot reach and monocular uncertainty. The 50° threshold preserves over half of the white demonstration's 88° relative turn despite the changed start heading and uncertain occluded pose. The 20° approach tolerance permits final upright correction during descent. Over the episode, the standard nearly-still-joint indicator may accumulate at most 25° passive relative rotation, half of the required relative turn. During the successful turn, require at least 35° of relative excursion accompanied by actual finger motion, estimated by composing relative-rotation increments when the 0.10 s mean norm of finger-joint speeds is at least 0.30 rad/s (the harness indicator). This is a motion proxy and can include contact rolling. Standard predicates are opposed_rel_rotation_deg >= 50, opposed_wrist_rotation_deg <= 65, and passive_rel_rotation_deg <= 25.
  3. Carry and release. With the same opposed grip after turning, enter the goal zone with blades within 20° of up while the plug is airborne. It must have moved at least 0.15 m toward +y from start before that entry. The white and black demonstrations travel 0.199 m and 0.212 m respectively, and the station's nearest permissible goal boundary is 0.25 m from the nominal start. Moving left may overlap the turn. Descend onto table support with hand contact and blades within 20° of vertical, then break contact while the plug is supported. This permits continuous support transfer and excludes dropping an airborne plug into the zone. Use the evaluator's ordered contact, position and axis checks plus standard touching_hand_at_end <= 0 and touching_environment_at_end >= 1.
  4. Placed. Apply the following exact condition over the final 0.5 s, using the object state-frame origin and standing height of -0.2935 m. Standard predicates also check final position, axis and contact. Evaluation verifies the full continuous sampled end window.

Success condition (given; include it unchanged in your criteria):

  • the plug's body centre is in the goal zone, x in [0.28, 0.48] m and y in [-0.10, 0.05] m;
  • it stands blades up: its +Z axis is within 10 deg of vertical;
  • its centre is at its standing height on the table within +-10 mm;
  • it is at rest: linear speed below 0.02 m/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s;
  • all of this holds over the last 0.5 s of the episode, and the hand does not touch it then.

Judge only episodes that satisfy all stages in order with no stop and no hardware violation. Attempts can restart after a missed grasp or drop. Carry and release must follow a qualifying lift and turn on the same attempt. The task suite requires at least 80% successful episodes across independent fixed-start position and heading draws and sensor seeds. This is the mastery requirement, allowing some failed episodes under the noisy sensor. Zero hardware violations are allowed. The feasibility suite requires at least 25% across the identical starts and criteria to demonstrate a physical path without making a robustness claim. The verification tests the single deployment plug and does not establish performance for the two-plug sequence or on hardware.

Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal. Add 20 ms to the joint reference delays as a lumped effective fit to command log and encoder timing. Published physical bounds are preserved. The DLS home-posture pull is 4e-5, calibrated against free-motion target arm encoders using [redacted]. The existing 100 Hz rate, measured IK seeds, 8 updates, damping, capsule barrier, joint limits, velocity limit and stop logic use the v6 implementation. The additional hand–table distance is isolated through hand–table pairs and does not apply to the arm capsules.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits with the contact margins and load response stated in the scene. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits with the contact margins and load response stated in the scene. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz sampling, 2 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive observation delay are preserved. The driving torque caps use each joint speed from RIGHT_HAND.md section 2 at every 1 ms substep. The opposite-direction cap retains the nominal braking torque. Contact can backdrive the joint past the published speed because the model does not clip joint velocity or angle. Hand–table pairs have 0.45 sliding friction, 0.013 s normal contact time, damping ratio 1 and an effective 5 mm additional contact distance. Training keeps the same mixed material rule for the pair response.

Limitations
The hand–table correction is effective fit distance and does not identify actual glove thickness. It improves early palm, object and torque residuals on the unseen [redacted] trajectories, while every first replay grasp…
more
The hand–table correction is effective fit distance and does not identify actual glove thickness. It improves early palm, object and torque residuals on the unseen [redacted] trajectories, while every first replay grasp still retains the plug at 2.00 s. `None` of the three target retry halts or two joint excursions is reproduced. [redacted] signed torque RMS slightly worsens. The 13 s CPU/Warp parity accepts a six-completion count difference on 128 draws. The kinematic demo replay places an illustrative robot aperture on a retargeted trajectory and can overlap the object in occluded phases.

physical_prior
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair…
more
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
contact
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static…
more
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static friction, table geometry and masses are preserved at the previous nominal values. Glove friction is 0.45. The three plug–table pairs use an explicit 1 mm effective contact margin to align supported pose height. The table plane and all plug mesh dimensions are fixed.
arm
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K)…
more
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal. Add 20 ms to the joint reference delays as a lumped effective fit to command log and encoder timing. Published physical bounds are preserved. The DLS home-posture pull is 4e-5, calibrated against free-motion target arm encoders using [redacted]. The existing 100 Hz rate, measured IK seeds, 8 updates, damping, capsule barrier, joint limits, velocity limit and stop logic use the v6 implementation. The additional hand–table distance is isolated through hand–table pairs and does not apply to the arm capsules.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz sampling, 2 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive observation delay are preserved. The driving torque caps use each joint speed from RIGHT_HAND.md section 2 at every 1 ms substep. The opposite-direction cap retains the nominal braking torque. Contact can backdrive the joint past the published speed because the model does not clip joint velocity or angle. Hand–table pairs have 0.45 sliding friction, 0.013 s normal contact time, damping ratio 1 and an effective 5 mm additional contact distance. Training keeps the same mixed material rule for the pair response.
sensor
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders.…
more
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.

Limitations
The fitted margin models effective supported separation from estimator readings. A camera vertical offset and contact separation are not independently observable in the stationary data. The open-loop dynamic residuals…
more
The fitted margin models effective supported separation from estimator readings. A camera vertical offset and contact separation are not independently observable in the stationary data. The open-loop dynamic residuals stay similar or worsen slightly. The measured torque halts and finger excursions remain unresolved. The specified flange payload mass exceeds that of the mounted model by about 0.339 kg. Two plausible additions worsened free-motion and contact torque residuals in matched replays, so this uses the effective v7 drive model. The kinematic reconstruction comparison illustrates finger aperture and can overlap the plug by 5.24 mm. Deepest overlap in the independent CPU actor sample is 0.534 mm. Closed-loop parity covers 13 s and complements the 60 s contract feasibility and task gates.

physical_prior
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair…
more
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
contact
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static…
more
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static friction, table geometry and masses are preserved at the previous nominal values. Glove friction is 0.45. The three plug–table pairs use an explicit 1 mm effective contact margin to align supported pose height. The table plane and all plug mesh dimensions are fixed.
arm
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K)…
more
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal. Add 20 ms to the joint reference delays as a lumped effective fit to command log and encoder timing. Published physical bounds are preserved. The DLS home-posture pull is 4e-5, calibrated against free-motion target arm encoders using [redacted]. The existing 100 Hz rate, measured IK seeds, 8 updates, damping, capsule barrier, joint limits, velocity limit and stop logic use the v6 implementation.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz sampling, 2 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive observation delay are preserved. The driving torque caps use each joint speed from RIGHT_HAND.md section 2 at every 1 ms substep. The opposite-direction cap retains the nominal braking torque. Contact can backdrive the joint past the published speed because the model does not clip joint velocity or angle.
sensor
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders.…
more
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.
revision
cause
The recorded supported plug starts in five target deliveries are around 0.95 mm above the zero-margin geometry. Upright ends with stable visibility show the same offset.
implementation
Use a 1 mm margin on the three explicit plug/table contact pairs in the shared MJCF. Hand–plug, arm/table and hand/table geometry, dimensions, controllers, stops, limits, sensor and criteria are the same as in v7.
evidence
r0860, the paired rounds 3–5 sent-command replays, 64 clean holds, a rendered reconstruction comparison and closed-loop CPU/Warp parity on 128 starts.
gpu_backend
physics
Same 1 ms plant, effort envelopes, model and actuator targets under Warp. Controller delay buffers hold the longest randomized delay. Delay, contact softness, friction and margin can vary between training worlds.
validation
r0787 paired deterministic closed-loop outcome audit over 13 s and 128 shared starts. CPU 121/128 and Warp 123/128, both with zero measured hardware faults, stops and drops. Parity PASS.

White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

Limitations
The IK fit compares measured encoder logs during the free approach. It does not identify all exposure, actuation and logging delays separately. Changing the home-pose term substantially improves the arm joint angles and…
more
The IK fit compares measured encoder logs during the free approach. It does not identify all exposure, actuation and logging delays separately. Changing the home-pose term substantially improves the arm joint angles and changes the closed-loop policy distribution. Palm, contact and torque residuals change little. The acute target torque halts and contact slips in r0686 and r0687 remain unresolved. The kinematic reference replay uses an illustrated aperture and can overlap the plug by 3.75 mm. The 13 s outcome parity comparison characterizes physics backend agreement and is shorter than the 60 s task gates. All five station stops in [redacted] also remain unexplained. The original v6 package recorded 62/64 in its own final gate.

The unchanged paced policy completes 42/64 development starts in the revised model, so training must adapt to that posture.

r0770: I viewed the turn failure and both successes. In seed 275518686 the plug is between the fingers at 2.30 s and looks upright by 10 s, but the qualifying turn is absent despite 78.8 degrees of measured opposed relative rotation. The v6 gate reacts sensitively to opposed posture. r0749 and the prospective r0772 feedback quantify an independent arm posture mismatch before contact. The small posture-pull correction improves that measured joint path with similar palm position.

method
White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its…
more
White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

Limitations
The replay identifies effective timing and part of the first-contact discrepancy. The physical drive and acquisition phase are confounded, arm joint RMS grows for some fitted cases, and the model still misses the…
more
The replay identifies effective timing and part of the first-contact discrepancy. The physical drive and acquisition phase are confounded, arm joint RMS grows for some fitted cases, and the model still misses the measured reaction torque peaks and contact transitions. Closed-loop paired rates agree more closely than the per-seed outcomes. Kinematic reference overlap reaches 3.75 mm. The model uses one white plug and nominally fixed table geometry as specified.

physical_prior
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair…
more
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
contact
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static…
more
Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static friction, table geometry and masses are preserved at the previous nominal values. Glove friction is 0.45.
arm
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K)…
more
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal. Add 20 ms to the joint reference delays as a lumped effective fit to command log and encoder timing. Published physical bounds are preserved.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz sampling, 2 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive observation delay are preserved. The driving torque caps use each joint speed from RIGHT_HAND.md section 2 at every 1 ms substep. The opposite-direction cap retains the nominal braking torque. Contact can backdrive the joint past the published speed because the model does not clip joint velocity or angle.

Limitations
The voltage-limited torque curve is assumed. Only the published speed, existing current-limit effort and prior unloaded response constrain it. The first breakpoint is a modeling assumption, and the two sensitivity…
more
The voltage-limited torque curve is assumed. Only the published speed, existing current-limit effort and prior unloaded response constrain it. The first breakpoint is a modeling assumption, and the two sensitivity breakpoints do not uniquely identify the real motor. Contact may still backdrive a joint beyond the listed speed. The kinematic replay has a 3.75 mm maximum nominal hand-object overlap. This simulation covers one deployed white plug. It does not establish real robot success.

The v4 final r0424 has one finger excursion of 22.81 mrad even though the manipulation stages pass. r0435 reproduces the same type of excursion after an inter-finger contact releases, with measured simulated PIP speed more than twice the public 12.863 rad/s. Current limiting alone leaves unrealistic motor power at that speed.

The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
contact
Housing and two blades have separate convex collision meshes. Elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solref 0.012 s / damping ratio 1, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001].
arm
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K)…
more
Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive delays are unchanged.
sensor
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders.…
more
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.
revision
cause
In r0287 the task gate rejects a measured hand limit excursion. The registered v3 stress audit finds violations on 13/24 starts, with no arm-limit excursion. Fine integration and stiffer unilateral joint constraints…
more
In r0287 the task gate rejects a measured hand limit excursion. The registered v3 stress audit finds violations on 13/24 starts, with no arm-limit excursion. Fine integration and stiffer unilateral joint constraints better enforce the specified deployed finger ranges without modifying encoder observations.
implementation
Reduce physics step from 2 ms to 1 ms and change only the 20 deployed finger limit solver time constants to 2 ms. The 100 Hz arm and hand controllers, 60 Hz sensor samples, 30 Hz policy rate and all ranges, stops,…
more
Reduce physics step from 2 ms to 1 ms and change only the 20 deployed finger limit solver time constants to 2 ms. The 100 Hz arm and hand controllers, 60 Hz sensor samples, 30 Hz policy rate and all ranges, stops, object, arm and criteria stay the same. Reproduce the substep timing in MuJoCo Warp.
evidence
r0271, r0287, r0290, r0303, r0309
gpu_backend
physics
Full geometry MuJoCo Warp 3.17 with the motor-limited arm and exactly timed 1 ms physics substeps over the 100 Hz controls and 60 Hz samples.
limitations
The 128-start finite-plan comparison passes outcome parity. Arithmetic, proprioception, pose randomness and contact sequences can still yield different episodes.

White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

Limitations
The kinematic replay has large positional errors and brief hand–plug overlap, and uses a visualization-only aperture. It is not evidence of physical feasibility. Ramp lag at the recommended start is 32.7 mm, above the…
more
The kinematic replay has large positional errors and brief hand–plug overlap, and uses a visualization-only aperture. It is not evidence of physical feasibility. Ramp lag at the recommended start is 32.7 mm, above the station example 18–25 mm, so the first action needs margin. No measured glove friction or plug mass from the station. Independent parity is pending for any parallel training backend.

physical_prior
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair…
more
The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
contact
Housing and two blades have separate convex collision meshes. Elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solref 0.012 s / damping ratio 1, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001].
arm
Measured-seed DLS IK, 1 and 0.2 position/rotation weights, eight updates per 100 Hz tick, a soft home preference and approach-to-column rejection using the collision capsules. Right arm 5-degree-margin limits, 20 mm and…
more
Measured-seed DLS IK, 1 and 0.2 position/rotation weights, eight updates per 100 Hz tick, a soft home preference and approach-to-column rejection using the collision capsules. Right arm 5-degree-margin limits, 20 mm and 0.075 rad per tick sent-target caps, published jump and box checks, per-joint command rate capped at 3.1416 rad/s. Models the joint-specific delay and low-pass response and impedance relative to command velocity. Joint torques use full physical contact generalized forces with a 30 ms external-torque estimator. The parked left side has its original collision masks.
hand
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation…
more
Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise.
sensor
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders.…
more
Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.
revision
Finger joint-limit constraints use a 4 ms time constant and [0.95,0.995,0.001] impedance. The original soft joint constraints produced excursions beyond the documented 0.02 rad allowance when the plug loaded the middle…
more
Finger joint-limit constraints use a 4 ms time constant and [0.95,0.995,0.001] impedance. The original soft joint constraints produced excursions beyond the documented 0.02 rad allowance when the plug loaded the middle finger. The deployed limits, controller targets, plate specification and numeric violation checks are identical.
gpu_backend
physics
MuJoCo Warp 3.17, full scene XML, current torque and stop checks, port of weighted MDH DLS controller. 3/4 ticks per policy step sample in a 60 Hz sensor schedule. Training backend uses TorchPoseSensorBatch with…
more
MuJoCo Warp 3.17, full scene XML, current torque and stop checks, port of weighted MDH DLS controller. 3/4 ticks per policy step sample in a 60 Hz sensor schedule. Training backend uses TorchPoseSensorBatch with matching default parameters and deterministic geometric visibility.
limitations
GPU floating-point and substep rounding can differ. Nominal hold test all 1024 stop-free, settled palm within 0.4 mm. Dynamic matched-seed parity is pending.

Hypotheses, decisions, reflections and blockers.

reflectionRetain the exact contract-v3 PPO package from r1202 and accepted gate r1232. The provided reconstruction r0002 and fixed criteria r0003 guided opposed acquisition, an active in-hand turn and…
more
Retain the exact contract-v3 PPO package from r1202 and accepted gate r1232. The provided reconstruction r0002 and fixed criteria r0003 guided opposed acquisition, an active in-hand turn and controlled supported release. The v10 feasibility gate gives 27 of 32. Independent final gate r1239 gives 63 of 64 with zero simulated hardware violations or stops, and the cumulative fresh suite gives 285 of 288. Final verification r1303 associates that exact model and manifest with the latest evidence. All 13 target rounds have judgments and sent-command replays. The exact retained package gives two clean target trials in [redacted] and one in [redacted], so target mastery remains unmet. The frozen v10 model retains all eight first grasps in [redacted] replay while two persist on the target. It also misses the two upper middle MCP2 excursions and the retry torque halt. The load-dependent middle contact calibration improved earlier held-out motion and preserved established replay paths. The later contact changes repair isolated support sequences and lose prior successful paths. The randomized-cap, loaded-opening and supported-slide PPO comparisons improve selected sensitivities and fail to displace the incumbent on the frozen suite. Given more target access, I would collect independent timed contact and actuator-response traces around the early supported displacement and the retry, then fit both finger-limit and arm-moment response against held-out starts. I would test the resulting first grasp and recovery trajectories before freezing a further simulator version. The measured target gaps and the verified simulation outcome are recorded separately.

They all preserve [redacted] trials 2 and 4 and all lose [redacted] trial 6. Short nominal closed-loop results range from 23 to 24 of 24 with no stops or hardware faults. The screen does not identify a support law that preserves earlier confirmed paths. No change is made to criteria, frozen evaluator or package. [redacted] median pose validity is 66.58 percent on target and 82.0 percent in replay.

Compare one final 1.5M PPO continuation from r1259 with a synthetic supported +X slide during approach. Draw 0.45–0.66 N on 35 percent of nonnominal full resets from 1.00–1.22 s, and apply only while the preceding 60 Hz sample reports support. The simulation keeps physical contacts and zeroes the disturbance once the plug leaves support.
